headline: Public Holiday Declared in Three Bagmati Districts for Chepang Community's Nwagi Festival
body:
The Bagmati provincial government has announced a public holiday across Chitwan, Makwanpur, and Dhading districts on Monday, Bhadra 22, to mark Nwagi (also known as Chhonam), the major cultural festival of the indigenous Chepang community.

The decision was officially published in the provincial Rajpatra by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Law. According to provincial authorities, the holiday aims to recognize and honor the cultural traditions of the Chepang community, who reside predominantly in these three districts.

Nwagi is a traditional harvest festival celebrated annually by the Chepang people, during which they offer their newly harvested crops and fruits to their ancestors before consuming them. By issuing the notice, the provincial government has ensured that community members and local residents in the affected areas can participate in the cultural celebrations.

headline: Kanchanpur Mobilizes Over Rs 10 Million for Flood Relief and Rehabilitation
body:
Kanchanpur has mobilized more than Rs 10 million in financial assistance for relief, rescue, and rehabilitation efforts following the devastating floods. The funds have been collected through contributions from local governments, institutions, organizations, businesses, and individuals and deposited into the Prime Minister’s Natural Disaster Relief Fund.

Among the major contributors, Shuklaphanta Municipality provided Rs 7 lakh, while Far-Western University contributed Rs 88 lakh collected through salary contributions from its faculty and staff members.

The Kanchanpur Industries and Commerce Association contributed Rs 5.25 lakh, while Little Buddha Academy donated Rs 8.25 lakh to support flood-affected communities.

Several local cooperatives and organizations have also extended financial assistance. Udayadev Cooperative Society, Megha Cooperative and other institutions have contributed to the relief effort.

Schools, businesses and other organizations across the district have also joined the fundraising campaign, with individual contributions ranging from Rs 51,000 to Rs 1 lakh.

Gurukul International School is further organizing a religious festival to raise additional funds for flood victims, adding another dimension to the community-led relief campaign.

The broad participation from government bodies, educational institutions, businesses, cooperatives and the wider community reflects Kanchanpur’s collective response to the disaster and its commitment to supporting affected families through relief and rehabilitation efforts.

headline: Sanima Reliance Life Insurance Contributes Rs. 72 Lakh to PM Disaster Relief Fund
body:
Sanima Reliance Life Insurance has contributed a total of Rs. 72 lakh to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support the rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and humanitarian assistance of people affected by the devastating floods that struck Rasuwa and other parts of the country on Bhadra 10, 2083.

Of the total contribution, Rs. 51 lakh was provided by the company, while Rs. 21 lakh was contributed by its directors and employees. The combined contribution was handed over to Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle through a single cheque.

The company expressed condolences to those who lost their lives and wished for the speedy recovery of the injured. It also called for continued cooperation and support from all stakeholders in ongoing rescue, relief, and rehabilitation efforts.

headline: Rs. 7 Arba 88 Lakhs Collected in PM Disaster Relief Fund, Balen Says
body:
Prime Minister Balen Shah has said that Rs. 7 Arba 88 Lakhs 57 Thousand 217 rupees has been collected in the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund so far. Speaking in Parliament, Shah said that several countries, including India, China, the United States, Japan, Bangladesh, the United Kingdom, Australia and South Korea etc., have provided financial and material support for disaster response and relief efforts in Nepal.

Shah said Indian, Chinese and Nepali tunnel experts are also working together in rescue operations involving tunnels. He further informed Parliament that 48 suspension bridges have been affected by the recent disasters, of which 28 need to be completely reconstructed while 20 require maintenance. Similarly, 31 motorable bridges have been swept away. The government is preparing to install Bailey bridges as soon as possible to restore road connectivity in the affected areas. 12 hydropower projects affected in which 8 were operational and 4 were in construction process.

headline: Reminder! Last Trading Day to Secure Dividend of Sunrise Focused Equity Fund and Sanima Growth Fund
body:
Today is the last day to grab the dividend proposed by

Sunrise Focused Equity Fund (SFEF).

At the 165th meeting of the Board of Directors of LS Capital Limited, the fund manager, held on Bhadra 05, 2083, the Board decided to distribute the 4.5% cash dividend to SFEF unitholders for fiscal year 2082/83.

body:

Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL).

headline: NEPSE Contributes Rs. 1.11 Crores to Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund for Bhotekoshi Flood Victims
body:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) has provided Rs. 1 crore 11 lakh 11 thousand 111 to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund to support relief and rescue efforts for communities affected by the devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi River.

The contribution was made under NEPSE’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative. NEPSE handed over a cheque for the amount to Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle during a programme held today.

The devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi River on Bhadra 10, 2083 caused extensive loss of life and property in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other affected areas.

The disaster resulted in significant damage to homes, infrastructure and livelihoods, leaving many communities in urgent need of assistance. Against this backdrop, NEPSE said its financial support was intended to help provide immediate relief to affected citizens and strengthen government-led rescue and recovery efforts.

The financial assistance will be used for immediate relief, medical treatment, and rehabilitation of people affected by the floods.

Finance Minister Dr. Wagle assured that the funds would be utilized transparently and effectively for the benefit of flood-affected communities. The government has emphasized the need to prioritize urgent humanitarian assistance and rehabilitation in areas severely impacted by the disaster.

NEPSE’s contribution adds to ongoing efforts by government agencies, financial institutions, businesses and other organizations to support communities affected by the Bhotekoshi floods.

headline: Arghakhanchi Cement Contributes Rs 675,000 to PM Disaster Relief Fund
body:
The Arghakhanchi Cement has extended financial assistance amounting to Rs 675,000 to support families affected by the recent Bhotekoshi flood and help with relief and rehabilitation efforts.

The amount, collected voluntarily by the employees of Arghakhanchi Cement, will be deposited in the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund, said Uddhav Karki, General Manager of Arghakhanchi Cement.

Karki said the employees came together to contribute at a time when many families are struggling to recover from the August 26's devastating flood. "During difficult times, we felt that we too should do something to help those in need.

The employees discussed the matter among themselves and voluntarily collected the money," he said. He added that this was the first time employees of the organization had spontaneously come together to raise such a substantial amount for people affected by a disaster.

headline: Gold Slips Below Rs. 3 Lakh, Silver Under Rs. 5,000
body:
Gold prices have witnessed a sharp fall in the domestic market today, falls by Rs. 8800 per tola to settle at Rs. 297,300 per tola, down from the previous rate of Rs. 306,100 per tola.

Federation of Nepal Gold and Silver Dealers' Association (FENEGOSIDA)

reported that Tejabi gold price also falls by Rs. 8800 per tola to reach Rs. 296,600 per tola, compared to Rs. 305,400 per tola on the previous day.

Similarly, Silver prices moves in the same direction, price falls by Rs. 185 now trading at Rs. 4,580 per tola down from previous rate Rs. 4,765 per tola.

headline: Decoding the Stocks Trading Above Rs. 2,000; Key EPS, P/E, and Floated Share Insights
body:
There are only a handful of companies on NEPSE whose share price currently trades above the Rs. 2,000 mark, making this a fairly exclusive group among all listed stocks. In this analysis, we have looked closely at these high priced companies to understand what stands behind their pricing. Alongside their current trading price, we have examined their 52 week high, the number of shares actually available for public trading, their earnings per share, and their price to earnings ratio.

Together, these numbers help explain why some of these stocks are priced the way they are, and whether that price is being supported by strong earnings or simply by a limited supply of shares in the market.

Companies above 2000 Price and their 52 Week High:

Unilever Nepal (UNL) is trading at Rs. 46,200, down more than 7% from its 52 week high, the shallowest decline among the group. Bottlers Nepal (BNL) stands at Rs. 14,405, down more than 14% from it's 52 week high price, while Rastriya Beema Company (RBCL) is at Rs. 13,388, down more than 17% from its 52 week high, showing a relatively deeper correction.

Companies above 2000 Price and their floated share:

Among the high priced stocks, Unilever Nepal (UNL) has the lowest floated shares at just 138,105, followed by Aatmanirbhar Laghubitta (ANLB) at 292,021 and Bottlers Nepal (Terai) Limited (BNT) at 302,500. These low public floats indicate relatively limited share availability in the market.

Companies above 2000 Price and their Earning Per Share:

Uniliver Nepal Limited (UNL) posts by far the highest EPS in this group at Rs. 1,712.27, which combined with its thin 138,105 share float and 85% promoter holding helps explain its elevated trading price of Rs. 46,200. Bottlers Nepal (Terai) (BNT) follows with an EPS of Rs. 544.86, the second highest in the list, supporting its relatively resilient price performance noted earlier. Bottlers Nepal Limited (Balaju) (BNL) comes third with an EPS of Rs. 419.57, rounding out the top three earners by a wide margin over the rest of the group.

Note: EPS was taken from companies Q4 report of F.Y. 2082/83

Companies above 2000 Price and their Price to Earning Ratio:

Bottlers Nepal (Terai) Limited (BNT) carries the lowest P/E ratio in this group at 21.23, making it the cheapest counter relative to earnings despite its high EPS of Rs. 544.86 noted earlier a combination that stands out as relatively attractively valued within this basket.

Uniliver Nepal (UNL) follows at 26.98, still comparatively modest given its exceptionally high EPS of Rs. 1,712.27, reinforcing that its elevated share price is earnings backed rather than purely speculative.

At the other end, Salt Trading (STC) and Reliance Spinning Mills (RSML) trade at the richest multiples, 133.09 and 129.71 respectively.

Note: P/E Ratio is calculated taking LTP of August 31, 2026 and F.Y. 2082/83 Q4 EPS report.

headline: Dev Group and Two Hydropower Companies Contribute Rs. 5 Million to Bhotekoshi Flood Relief Fund
body:
Dev Group, United Mewa Khola Hydropower Limited, and United Modi Hydropower Limited have jointly provided Rs. 5 million to support relief and rehabilitation efforts for communities affected by the devastating floods and landslides in Rasuwa’s Bhotekoshi River area.

Dev Group Chairman Narendra Ballabh Pant and Managing Director Ajay Ballabh Pant handed over the assistance to Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha for deposit into the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund.

The companies said the contribution will help provide immediate relief and support rehabilitation of disaster-affected citizens. They also expressed their commitment to continuing support for affected communities and humanitarian initiatives in the coming days.

headline: Nepal Rastra Bank Urges Banks to Facilitate Financial Services for Natural Disaster-Affected Customers
body:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has directed banks and financial institutions to facilitate access to banking services for customers affected by the recent natural disasters in Rasuwa and other districts.

The central bank issued the notice after reports that customers affected by the disasters have lost essential banking documents and instruments, including cheques, bank cards, mobile banking access and other necessary documents.

NRB has requested banks and financial institutions to make necessary arrangements to identify affected customers using the signature specimens, photographs and other customer details already available with the institution.

The measure is intended to help customers continue or resume essential banking transactions even when they are unable to produce their usual identification documents or banking instruments due to the disaster.

The central bank has emphasized the need to provide necessary assistance and facilitation to disaster-affected customers under the difficult circumstances.

The directive aims to ensure that people affected by the recent floods, landslides, and other natural disasters are not deprived of essential financial services simply because their banking documents or access instruments were lost or damaged.

NRB has called on concerned banks and financial institutions to adopt necessary arrangements to ensure continued access to banking and financial services for affected customers during the crisis.

headline: Know How Did The Mutual Funds Perform in Shrawan, A Complete Analysis of Multiple Factors
body:
There are currently 46 closed-end mutual funds listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange, whereas 14 open-end schemes

which are traded directly with the respective fund manager, in which there will be 60 schemes altogether.

Click here for a detailed list of Mutual funds:

Mutual Fund Schemes have an accumulative investment in listed/unlisted companies of Rs. 68.19 Arba in the month of Shrawan, 2083, compared to Rs. 67.44 Arba in Ashad, 2083.

Similarly, the mutual fund bank balance increased to Rs. 14.31 Arba in Shrawan from Rs. 13.25 Arba in Ashad. Mutual Funds have invested in debentures and bonds amounting to Rs. 4.70 Arba. Similarly, the funds have also invested 1.00% in primary shares/Rights, which amounts to Rs. 89.51 crores.

Mutual funds had significant holdings in various sectors as of the end of Shrawan. Investment in the commercial banking industry accounts for the highest sector-wise investment of Rs. 13.78 Arba, making up 20.25% of total investment. Likewise, they have an investment of Rs. 11.17 Arba in shares of the Hydropower sector, for 16.42% of the total investment. The Microfinance sector stands at the third-highest investment priority for mutual funds, with an investment worth Rs. 7.41 Arba, contributing 10.90% of total investments.

Smaller allocations were observed in sectors like manufacturing and products, promoter share, and others. These sector-wise holdings provide insight into the diversification strategies employed by mutual funds and their preferences for sector exposure.

Among the commercial banks, Everest Bank Limited (EBL) is seen as the top priority for investment mutual funds. It accounts for an investment worth Rs. 1.97 Arba. Sanima Bank Limited (SANIMA) stands in second place with an of Rs. 1.59 Arba. Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) stands in the third position with an investment of Rs. 1.30 arba.

As for the development banks, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the highest investment preference among mutual funds. The mutual funds have invested an amount worth Rs. 1.57 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) is seen in the second position with an investment worth Rs. 1.08 Arba. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has an investment of Rs. 1.05 Arba in the third position.

As for the finance companies, the top two investments were ICFC Finance Limited (ICFC) and Manjushree Finance Limited (MFIL). Mutual funds invested Rs. 24.89 Crores in ICFC and Rs. 10.39 Crores in MFIL.

Among the Seven listed hotels and the tourism sector in NEPSE, mutual funds have given higher priority to Soaltee Hotel Limited (SHL) with an investment of Rs. 73.57 crores.

The inclination of investment in hydropower companies for mutual funds was in Mountain Energy Nepal Limited (MEN) with an investment of Rs. 1.53 arba, with an investment of Sahas Urja Limited (SAHAS) of Rs. 1.22 arba, and Api Power Company Limited (API) with an investment of Rs. 1.06 arba.

Among the life insurance companies in Nepal, National Life Insurance Company Limited (NLICL), Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC), and Asian Life Insurance Company Limited (ALICL) are the top priority investment companies for mutual funds. Mutual Fund schemes have around Rs. 1.79 Arba in investments in NLICL, Rs. 1.72 Arba in investments in NLIC, and Rs. 82.54 crore in ALICL.

Among the listed microfinance companies, Chhimek Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (CBBL), Sana Kisan Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (SKBBL) and Nirdhan Utthan Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (NUBL) were the top three investment priorities for mutual funds. Mutual Funds invested Rs. 1.77 Arba in CBBL, Rs. 1.13 Arba in SKBBL, and Rs. 93.35 crores in NUBL.

The mutual fund schemes also invest in other mutual funds. Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana (NSY) falls under the highest investment value mutual fund. It has an investment of Rs. 22.21 crores. NIC Asia Growth Fund 2 (NICGF2) has the second-highest equity fund with a value of Rs. 18.39 crores. Finally, NIBL Stable Fund (NIBLSTF) stood as the third-highest investment of Rs. 16.04 crores.

Among the non-life insurance companies in Nepal, Siddhartha Premier Insurance Limited (SPIL), Neco Insurance Company Limited (NIL) and Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Company Limited (SALICO), are the investment companies of top priority for mutual funds. Mutual Fund schemes have around Rs. 1.46 Arba investments in SPIL, Rs. 1.30 Arba in NIL and Rs. 1.16 Arba in SALICO.

Similarly, the promoter share as per the choice of mutual funds are:

As for the other sector, mutual funds have invested Rs. 78.85 crores in Himalayan Reinsurance Limited (HRL), and Rs. 73.16 crores in Nepal Reinsurance Company Limited (NRIC).

As for the Investment sector, Citizen Investment Trust (CIT) has the highest investment worth Rs. 1.03 arba. Similarly, CEDB Hydropower Development Company Limited (CHDC) stands in the second position with an investment of Rs. 42.69 crores.

NAV stands for Net Asset Value, which represents a fund’s per-unit market value. Investors use this value to transact a particular mutual fund in the market. Since the NAV is calculated by subtracting all the liabilities from the total value of all the assets in a portfolio, the value changes following the change in their asset and liabilities.

In the month of Jestha, 2083, Machhapuchchhre SIP Yojana (MSIP) NAV lossed the highest by 5.05%. Conversely, NMB Saral Bachat Fund - E (NMBSBF) lossed the least by 4.53%.

headline: Butwal Power Company Group Contributes Rs 51.42 Lakhs to Bhote Koshi Flood Relief Fund
body:
Butwal Power Company Limited (BPCL), its group companies and employees have contributed Rs 51.41 lakhs to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund to support people affected by the devastating Bhote Koshi floods in Rasuwa. The cheque was handed over to Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha through the Independent Power Producers Association Nepal (IPPAN), in support of the government’s ongoing search, rescue and relief efforts.

Of the total contribution, BPCL and its employees contributed Rs 33.36 lakhs, including Rs 22 lakhs from the company and Rs 11.36 lakhs from management and employees. Other contributions included Nyadi Hydropower Rs 5.5 lakhs, Himal Power Rs 5 lakhs, Hydro Consult Engineering Rs 5.05 lakhs and Khudi Hydropower Rs 2.5 lakhs. The company also expressed condolences to those who lost their lives in the floods and wished for the safe recovery and contact of those still missing.

headline: Aashutosh Energy Limited Retains BBB- Credit Rating from ICRA Nepal
body:
ICRA Nepal Limited has reaffirmed the [ICRANP-IR] BBB- issuer rating of Aashutosh Energy Limited (AEL), indicating a moderate degree of safety in the timely servicing of financial obligations.

The rating reflects the general creditworthiness of the company and not any specific debt instrument. In ICRA’s rating scale, a “BBB-” is one notch below “BBB” and one notch above “BB+,” showing its relative position within the investment-grade category.

headline: Vivo V80 Lite Set to Launch in Nepal with 7,050mAh Battery
body:
Vivo has offered an early look at it's upcoming V80 Lite smartphone, confirming it's imminent arrival in Nepal.

Built around a "Slay Every Edge" design concept, the V80 Lite features a curved, ultra-slim unibody body, a Skyline Camera Design inspired by a bird in flight, and a Silk White finish with a satin dual-plating texture.

The device is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 7360-Turbo chip (4nm), paired with a 7050 mAh battery. Vivo says the phone will deliver a "50-month smooth experience," backed by three generations of OS upgrades and five years of security updates. For mobile gamers, it promises stable 90 FPS gameplay for up to three hours in MLBB, even at 30°C.

The display is a 1.5K Ultra Clear AMOLED panel, aimed at both entertainment and business use. On the camera front, the V80 Lite sports a 32 MP wide-angle front camera for group selfies, and a 50 MP Sony sensor rear camera with Clear Night Portrait mode for low-light shots.

Vivo has yet to announce pricing or a specific launch date for the Nepali market.

headline: Eastern Hydropower Receives Amended Regulatory Approval to Issue 54 Lakh Right Shares
body:
Eastern Hydropower Limited has received prior approval from the Electricity Regulatory Commission (ERC) to issue 54 lakhs right shares to its existing shareholders.

The company said the approval follows a decision made at its 9th Annual General Meeting (AGM) to issue right shares equivalent to its current paid-up capital on a 1:1 ratio.

Eastern Hydropower had initially submitted an application to the Electricity Regulatory Commission seeking prior approval to issue 6.2 million right shares, equivalent to 100% of its current paid-up capital of Rs. 62 Crores.

However, through a letter dated Bhadra 8, 2083, the Commission granted prior approval for the issuance of right shares at a revised ratio of 1:0.871, amounting to 5,400,092.743 shares with a proposed value of approximately Rs. 54.009 crores.

The company has now received another letter from the Electricity Regulatory Commission, dated Bhadra 17, 2083, providing prior approval, with certain amendments, to issue 54 lakhs right shares at the 1:0.871 ratio.

The total value of the approved right share issue stands at Rs. 54.00 Crores, with each share carrying a face value of Rs. 100.

The proposed right share issue will increase the company's paid-up capital and provide additional funds for its business and project-related requirements, subject to the remaining regulatory and issuance procedures.

headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Signs MoU with Federation of Transporter-Nepal to Facilitate Vehicle and Business Loans
body:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Federation of Transporter-Nepal (FTN) to provide financing support to transport businesses affiliated with the federation.

Under the agreement, FTN members can obtain loans from the bank to purchase vehicles of any brand required for transportation services and to meet their business financing needs. The bank will provide the loan facility through its 176 branches at attractive concessional interest rates.

The partnership is expected to make financial services more accessible to transport entrepreneurs, helping them expand their services and businesses. The bank has also introduced special loan offers at minimum interest rates for auto, agriculture and SME loans.

The MoU was signed by Tara Manandhar, Chief Executive Officer of Muktinath Bikas Bank, and Madhav Prasad Nepal, President of the Federation of Transporter-Nepal.

headline: NEPSE Continues its Upward Movement, Climbs 15.44 Points to Settle at 2,538.11 Level
body:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) recorded a double-digit gain today, gaining by 15.44 points (0.61%) to close at 2,538.11. This follows a 9.24 -point gain in the previous trading session.

The benchmark index opened at 2,524.23 and fluctuated between an intraday high of 2,538.18 and a low of 2,513.35 before settling at the close. Total turnover for the day amounted to Rs. 2.94 Arba, with 7,268,202 shares traded across 354 companies through 39,673 transactions. The total market capitalization stood at Rs. 43.65 Kharba, with a float market capitalization of Rs. 14.72 Kharba.

Sanima Middle Tamor Hydropower Limited (TAMOR) topped the turnover chart, recording transactions worth Rs. 14.17 crores. The company’s stock closed at Rs. 504.00.

Upakar Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (ULBSL) hit the upper circuit with a 11.87% gain. The stock closed at Rs. 2,790.00 .

Meanwhile, NMB Energy Bond 4% - 2093/94 (NMBUR93/94) recorded the Highest fall, falling by 5.81%. The last traded price of the company was Rs. 941.00.

Among sectors, Hydropower Index recorded the highest gain, gaining by 0.95%, while the Mutual Fund recorded the highest loss, down 0.09%.

headline: Schools in Flood Hit Areas in Nuwakot Closed for Indefinite Period
body:
Schools, affected by flood in Trishuli River following Bhotekoshi flash flood, have been closed for indefinite period in Nuwakot district. All the schools located in most flood hit Bidur municipality as well as Kispang rural municipality have remained closed while there is uncertainty to resume teaching learning activities in schools in other flood-hit areas.

Mayor of Bidur municipality, Rajan Shrestha, shared that there is no preparation to open schools immediately as students, teachers and parents are missing, school structures, roads and bridges have been damaged due to flood. The schools would be reopened only if daily life of the people become easier some extent and people could easily cross the river.

Education Section Chief of the municipality, Naba Raj Sapkota, mentioned that the scale of damage caused by flood became massive after being failed to imagine its impact though information about the flood was received. However, some schools managed to avert huge incident by exercising high-level cautions, he opined. "The current situation and daily life is not normal. We will make a plan to conduct teaching learning activities through alternative medium after some times," he stressed.

Out of 83 schools in Bidur municipality, one dozen of schools have been directly affected. As per the data of Education Section, four school buildings suffered fully damages. As per preliminary data prepared by Education Development and Coordination Unit, Nuwakot, there is no situation to run schools in previous places as the flood has damaged all structures of Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School, Ramchandra Basic School, Chetana Basic School and Trishuli Community Boarding School. Similarly, three blocks and hostel building of Uttargaya English Boarding School have been completely damaged.

Difficulties have surfaced in running teaching learning activities as the hostel of Chandeshwori Secondary School, where visually impaired students were residing, as well as Sahid Jagat Prakash Jung Shah Sanskrit Secondary School and Pioneer English Boarding areas have been damaged. A school bus of Ramchandra Basic School and two buses of Uttargaya English Boarding School have been washed away by flood. Likewise, though the flood has not caused damages to school buildings at Kispang rural municipalities, two school buildings have been set up as holding centres and one school at Belkotgadhi.

Shila Devi Secondary School located at Belkotgadhi-7 and Mahadev Secondary School at Belkotgadhi-5 have also been affected by flood.

headline: Shangrila Development Bank Contributes Rs 70 Lakhs for Bhotekoshi Flood Relief
body:
Shangrila Development Bank has deposited Rs 70 Lakhs to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support victims of the Bhotekoshi flood, which killed hundreds and displaced numerous families on Bhadra 10.

Of the total amount, Rs 50 Lakhs came from the bank's corporate social responsibility fund, while employees contributed Rs 20 Lakhs. Bank CEO Suyog Shrestha handed over the cheque to Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle.

The flood, which struck the Bhotekoshi River, left several people missing and caused damage worth billions of rupees. The bank extended condolences to the families of those who lost their lives in the disaster.

The funds are intended to support search and rescue operations, relief distribution, and long-term rehabilitation and reconstruction for affected communities.

Shangrila Development Bank currently operates 109 branches and 30 ATMs across the country, and said it remains committed to expanding its services while upholding strong governance, risk management, and internal control practices.

headline: Esewa Money Transfer Waives Remittance Fees to Support Rasuwa Flood Victims
body:
Esewa Money Transfer has fully waived service fees for remittances sent to Nepal from several countries following the devastating floods and landslides that affected the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa on Bhadra 10.

The initiative aims to enable Nepalis living abroad to send 100% of their intended funds safely and quickly to families and relatives in Nepal without any additional charges during the disaster.

The fee-free service is being provided in partnership with major international digital remittance partners, including Smith Transfer App in Romania, Panda Remit in Australia, the US, Japan, Hong Kong and Singapore, Merchantrade in Malaysia, Remitly across Europe, Australia, the US and UK, Fonemoney in South Korea, and Orbit Remit in New Zealand.

In addition, individuals and organizations abroad can send donations directly to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund through Esewa Money Transfer without service charges.

According to Ajesh Koirala, Chief Executive Officer of Esewa Money Transfer, the initiative is intended to ensure that the full amount sent by Nepalis abroad reaches affected families and relief efforts without deductions or delays. The company said it is coordinating with international partners to facilitate timely financial assistance during the crisis.

headline: Tourism Sector Suffers Over Rs 50 Billion Losses from Bhotekoshi Flooding: Minister Paudel
body:
Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadak Raj Paudel, has stated that a preliminary estimation has been made that the tourism sector has suffered losses more than Rs 50 billion from Bhotekoshi flash flood. Minister Paudel shared that the flood damaged 142 hotels, 57 restaurants and 141 vehicles related with tourism business as well as various important religious and cultural heritages of affected areas suffered damages.

He underlined that a situation has surfaced to find out an alternative routes as Langtang, Gosainkunda, Parbatikunda and Nathali trekking route have been damaged. Sharing that a plan has been forwarded through the ministry to develop flood-hit areas as 'climate heritage', the Tourism Minister opined that a decision was taken based on the discussion with stakeholders on the issues of constructing museum, park, monument, and other structures there.

He added that the Nepal has had to face a huge disaster due to climate change, stating that Nepalis have been facing consequences of a mistake the Nepal did not commit. Minister Paudel laid emphasis that the international community should provide necessary assistance and technology to Nepal affected from climate change, adding Nepal needs modern technology capable for providing early warnings before disaster regarding the risk posed by glacial lakes in Himalayan regions. He opined that initiatives would be taken with international community to provide such technologies being used in different countries of the world.

Nepali airline companies and helicopter promoters have made significant contributions in rescue and relief during flood, which is the significant contribution towards the nation, the Tourism Minister underscored. He thanked the hotel entrepreneurs for making arrangement of free accommodation and food to flood-hit people in different places including Pokhara, Chitwan and Kathmandu. Minister Paudel said that the government has started the process of setting up 'desks' at Tribhuvan International Airport and other necessary places to assist affected tourists and their families, and informed that coordination on this matter is ongoing with various ministries and embassies.

He said that effective communication at the international level is necessary to prevent negative messages about Nepal's tourism sector due to the disasters. The Tourism Minister suggested spreading the message worldwide that Nepal is safe and its tourism industry is ready to welcome any international visitor. "Natural disasters can happen anywhere in the world. They cannot destroy Nepal's tourism industry. We are still standing and ready to welcome tourists," he added. Minister Paudel pointed out that it is necessary to inform the international community about the suffering Nepal is facing due to climate change, and on the other hand, to send a message that Nepal is safe and open for tourism.

He also mentioned that a decision has been made to operate a welfare fund related to workers in the tourism sector and informed that coordination is underway with the Ministry of Finance regarding the complications that may arise in insurance claims when the exact status of people missing due to the flood is not known. Tourism Minister Paudel also stated that during national disasters, Nepali society usually comes together beyond politics, and this time too, the same social unity was seen in the rescue and relief efforts.

headline: Moderate Rainfall Forecast in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading
body:
Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading are likely to receive moderate rainfall today, while the possibility of heavy rain in these districts remains low, according to the Meteorological Forecasting Division.

Meteorologist Sanjeev Adhikari said the chances of heavy rainfall in the three districts are currently considered low. The monsoon remains active across the country, with a low-pressure system positioned slightly north of its average location in the western region and near its average position in the east.

The entire country is expected to remain predominantly cloudy this afternoon. Moderate rainfall and snowfall are likely in some Himalayan and hilly areas, with thunderstorms and lightning possible in certain locations.

The weather forecast also indicates a possibility of heavy rainfall at some locations in Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces. Similar conditions are possible in the hilly areas of Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces.

Authorities have advised people in areas prone to heavy rainfall to remain alert and follow the latest weather updates.

headline: Nepal Chamber of Commerce Urges Restraint from Businesses Amid Post-Flood Supply Disruptions
body:
The Nepal Chamber of Commerce has called on industrialists and businesspeople to trade responsibly and with restraint, citing disruptions to supply chains, transportation and trade caused by the recent devastating floods. The chamber issued the appeal through a statement on Monday.

With major festivals including Teej, Dashain, Tihar, Chhath, Nepal Sambat and Ramadan approaching, the chamber urged businesses to maintain regular supply of essential goods, avoid artificial shortages and price hikes, and prioritise consumer interests as market demand rises.

The chamber noted that the floods caused significant loss of life and property, along with serious disruption to transportation, supply chains and market operations. It said the damage to the northern Rasuwagadhi border point in particular has hampered imports, exports and goods supply, making it all the more necessary to keep markets functioning smoothly and in an orderly manner ahead of the festival season.

Calling on industrialists, importers, distributors, and wholesale and retail traders to conduct their business responsibly, the chamber stressed the need to use alternative supply routes where highways remain blocked, and to manage adequate storage and effective distribution systems.

The chamber said the private sector should undertake joint preparations to prevent disruptions in the supply of essential goods. It added that businesses should rise above profit motives to fulfil their social responsibility during the crisis, the government should focus on facilitation rather than control, and consumers should avoid unnecessary panic buying and hoarding.

No one should use the disruption caused by the disaster as an opportunity for unfair business gain, the chamber said, adding that the private sector must instead play a responsible role in maintaining market confidence during this difficult period.

headline: NRB to Collect 18 Billion from BFI's; Interest and Deposits Returns after 3 Month
body:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has announced that it will collect deposits worth Rs. 18 billion from banks and financial institutions through a bidding process today.

According to a notice published today, the central bank will collect the deposits for a period of 90 days. The bidding will take place on Bhadra 18 (September 03) through the Online Bidding System at 3 Pm.

The interest rate will be decided through the bidding process. The minimum amount for bidding has been set at Rs. 10 crore, while the maximum limit is (In multiples of) 5 Crore, up to the total issue amount. However, institutions can submit multiple bids within the total announced amount.

Only licensed ‘A’, ‘B’, and ‘C’ class banks and financial institutions approved by NRB are allowed to take part in the bidding. The deposits collected will be returned along with interest on Mangsir 16, 2083 (December 02, 2026).

headline: Chairman of Himalayan Reinsurance Limited Resigns
body:
The Chairman of the Board of Directors of Himalayan Reinsurance Limited, Uday Kumar Niroula, has resigned from his post, citing personal reasons.

headline: Himalayan Laghubitta Contributes Rs 5 Lakh for Bhotekoshi Flood Relief
body:
Himalayan Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited

has contributed Rs. 5,00,000 to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts for those affected by the devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi River on Bhadra 10.

The institution expressed deep grief over the extensive loss of life and property across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and neighbouring districts, offering condolences to the families of those who died and wishing a speedy recovery to the injured.

It also expressed sympathy for the hardship faced by people, including government and institutional employees and their families, who lost contact with loved ones during the disaster.

The institution thanked government agencies, local bodies, security forces, social organisations and volunteers involved in the ongoing rescue and relief operations, and reaffirmed its commitment to standing with affected communities during this difficult time.

headline: Flash Flood Risk Persists in Bhotekoshi and Trishuli River Systems
body:
The risk of flash floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems remains high today, with water levels expected to rise amid ongoing rainfall and the possibility of further precipitation in the upstream areas of the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa.

Saraswati Bista, a flood expert at the Flood Forecasting Division under the Centre of Hydrology and Water Resources Research, said water levels in the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli and surrounding rivers are likely to increase today.

The Division has urged residents living along riverbanks in Rasuwa and Nuwakot to remain highly alert due to the possibility of flash floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.

According to Bista, rising water levels could trigger moderate flash floods in rivers and streams across several districts. These include Taplejung, Panchthar, Tehrathum, Sankhuwasabha, Dhankuta, Bhojpur, Solukhumbu, Okhaldhunga, Khotang, Udayapur, Dolakha, Ramechhap, Sindhuli, Sindhupalchok, Kavrepalanchok, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur, Kathmandu, Dhading, Makawanpur, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu, Lamjung, Manang, Mustang, Myagdi, Kaski, Syangja, Parbat and Dolpa, along with nearby areas.

The Division has also warned that water levels in smaller rivers and streams could rise significantly in Rukum East, Rukum West, Salyan, Jajarkot, Surkhet, Dailekh, Kalikot, Mugu, Humla, Jumla, Achham, Bajhang, Bajura, Dadeldhura, Baitadi, Darchula and Kanchanpur. A moderate risk of sudden flooding has been forecast in these areas.

The Division has advised people living near riverbanks and those travelling along rivers and streams to remain cautious and closely monitor weather and flood updates, as sudden rises in water levels and flash floods are possible in small rivers and streams.

headline: Nabil Bank Appoints Global IME Capital as Issue Manager for Rs. 4 Arba Debenture
body:
has appointed Global IME Capital Limited as the issue manager for its upcoming "5.5% Nabil Debenture 2093".

The agreement was signed on Tuesday by Manoj Kumar Gyawali, Chief Executive Officer of Nabil Bank, and Mandeep Luitel, Chief Executive Officer of Global IME Capital.

Under the issue, Nabil Bank will issue 40 lakhs units debentures worth Rs. 4 Arba, with a face value of Rs. 1,000 each. The debentures will have a 10-year maturity period and carry an annual interest rate of 5.5%.

Of the total issue, 24 lakhs units worth Rs. 2.40 arba will be sold through private placement. The remaining 16 lakhs units worth Rs. 1.60 Arba will be offered to the general public. Of the public issue, 5% will be reserved for mutual funds.

Nabil Bank is one of Nepal’s major private-sector commercial banks, serving more than 2.6 million customers through a network of 263 branches and 315 ATMs across the country. The bank has been operating in Nepal’s banking sector for more than four decades.

headline: Ather Opens 13th Experience Center in Dharan, Records 25+ Bookings Before Launch
body:
Ather has expanded its presence in Nepal with the opening of its 13th Experience Center at Chata Chowk, Dharan-1, on Bhadra 17, 2083.

The new outlet will showcase Ather’s 450 series, 450X Overtone Series and Rizta, with customers able to take test rides and experience the scooter's features.

Ather said it received more than 25 bookings even before the center’s official opening. As part of the launch, customers can choose an extended battery warranty, 50% down payment at 0% interest, or an additional NPR 8,000 valuation until Bhadra 23.

The company currently has 10+ authorized service centers and more than 50 fast-charging points across Nepal. Ather’s Nepal operations are managed by authorized distributor Vaidya Energy Pvt. Ltd.

headline: Nepal Insurers Association Contribute Rs.3.47 Crores to Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund
body:
The Nepal Insurers Association has contributed Rs.3.47 crores to the government’s flood relief and reconstruction efforts following the devastating floods in Bhotekoshi on Bhadra 10.

A delegation led by Association Chairman Manohar Das Mul presented the contribution to Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle on Bhadra 17 in the presence of chairpersons and chief executive officers of participating insurance companies.

The contribution came from the association and eight non-life insurance companies, including Siddhartha Premier Insurance Co. Ltd., Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Co. Ltd., Nepal Insurance Ltd., Neco Insurance Ltd., Prabhu Insurance Ltd., United Ajod Insurance Ltd., Sanima GIC Insurance Ltd. and Himalayan Everest Insurance Co. Ltd.

Employees of Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance, Himalayan Everest Insurance and United Ajod Insurance also contributed Rs. 26,23,018, which was handed over along with the main contribution.

NLG Insurance and IGI Prudential Insurance had already provided financial assistance, while other non-life insurers are also preparing to contribute.

The association said insurers would prioritize claim settlements for damaged projects, infrastructure, property and other insured assets once loss details are received. Finance Minister Wagle thanked the insurance sector for its support during the crisis.

headline: Maya Khola Hydropower Company Limited Receives Preliminary Approval from ERC to Issue Right Shares at the Ratio of 1: 1
body:
Maya Khola Hydropower Company Limited (MKHC)

has received preliminary approval from the Electricity Regulatory Commission to issue a 1:1 rights offering.

The hydropower company proposed to issue 100% right shares on the paid-up capital of Rs. 1 Arba. After the adjustment of the proposed right shares, i.e., 1,00,00,000 units, the paid-up capital of the company will increase to Rs. 2.00 arba.

The company is issuing the right shares to complete the construction of the hydropower project and to pay other outstanding construction-related expenses.

The company will issue the right shares to its shareholders only after the approval of SEBON. As of writing, MKHC has an LTP of Rs. 250.00.

headline: NEPSE Extends Gains for Third Straight Session; Investment Index Leads Sectoral Gains
body:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) recorded a single-digit gain today, gaining by 4.66 points (0.18%) to close at 2,542.77. This follows a 15.44 -point gain in the previous trading session.

The benchmark index opened at 2,536.96 and fluctuated between an intraday high of 2,545.04 and a low of 2,533.28 before settling at the close. Total turnover for the day amounted to Rs. 3.46 Arba, with 12,163,763 shares traded across 346 companies through 39,673 transactions. The total market capitalization stood at Rs. 43.73 Kharba, with a float market capitalization of Rs. 14.74 Kharba.

Reliance Spinning Mills Limited (RSML) topped the turnover chart, recording transactions worth Rs. 40.90 crores. The company’s stock closed at Rs. 2,830.00.

Wean Nepal Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (WNLB) hit the upper circuit with a 8.76% gain. The stock closed at Rs. 1,055.00.

Meanwhile, Pure Energy Limited (PURE) recorded the Highest fall, falling by 13.33%. The last traded price of the company was Rs. 662.0.

Among sectors, Investment Index recorded the highest gain, gaining by 1.26%, while the Others Index recorded the highest loss, down 0.36%.

NEPSE Extends Gains for Third Straight Session; Investment Index Leads Sectoral Gains

Thu, Sep 3, 2026 3:48 PM on Highlight News, Stock Market,
-ShareSansar

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) recorded a single-digit gain today, gaining by 4.66 points (0.18%) to close at 2,542.77. This follows a 15.44 -point gain in the previous trading session.

 

The benchmark index opened at 2,536.96 and fluctuated between an intraday high of 2,545.04 and a low of 2,533.28 before settling at the close. Total turnover for the day amounted to Rs. 3.46 Arba, with 12,163,763 shares traded across 346 companies through 39,673 transactions. The total market capitalization stood at Rs. 43.73 Kharba, with a float market capitalization of Rs. 14.74 Kharba.

 

Reliance Spinning Mills Limited (RSML) topped the turnover chart, recording transactions worth Rs. 40.90 crores. The company’s stock closed at Rs. 2,830.00.

 

Wean Nepal Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (WNLB) hit the upper circuit with a 8.76% gain. The stock closed at Rs. 1,055.00.

Meanwhile, Pure Energy Limited (PURE) recorded the Highest fall, falling by 13.33%. The last traded price of the company was Rs. 662.0.

 

 

Among sectors, Investment Index recorded the highest gain, gaining by 1.26%, while the Others Index recorded the highest loss, down 0.36%.

108 companies currently in the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) pipeline

, seeking approval to issue a combined

. The latest pipeline was published by SEBON on August 18, 2026.

The situation has drawn further attention following the appointment of

Dr. Gopal Prasad Bhatta as SEBON chairperson

. Bhatta took the oath of office on June 19, 2026, after being appointed by the Cabinet.

Despite the appointment of the new chairperson,

no company has received IPO approval from SEBON since Bhatta took charge

, according to SEBON’s publicly available IPO approval records. The last IPO approval was issued on April 27, 2026, according to the regulator’s approval records. No new IPO has been approved since then.

This is only a mathematical estimate and does not represent SEBON’s official approval timeline. The actual period could be longer because new companies may continue to submit applications while existing proposals are under review.

The approval process must also be viewed against Nepal’s government working calendar. The Ministry of Home Affairs lists government office hours from

, with Saturdays and officially declared public holidays excluded from regular working days.

Therefore, if IPO approvals are processed strictly based on working days rather than a fixed weekly rate, public holidays and non-working days could further affect the pace of processing. The growing pipeline has left retail investors waiting for fresh primary-market opportunities, while the continued entry of new applications could further increase the backlog.

With 108 companies currently awaiting approval and no new IPO approved since the appointment of the new SEBON chairperson, the key concern for the market is how quickly the regulator will begin clearing the accumulated queue.

At a rate of just one approval per week, clearing the existing 108 companies would take 108 weeks, or more than two years. However, the actual timeline could be longer if new applications continue to enter the pipeline, making timely regulatory decisions crucial for both companies seeking to raise capital and investors waiting for new investment opportunities.

headline: NCP leader Barsha Man Pun Meets with PM Shah
body:
Nepali Communist Party (NCP) leader Barsha Man Pun called on Prime Minister Balendra Shah today. During the meeting held at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, Singha Durbar, they discussed the issues related to Bhotekoshi river flood, search, rescue and treatment of the affected people and relief distribution, shared PM Shah's Press and Research Expert, Dipa Dahal.

Discussion was also held the matter of bringing the infrastructures affected by Bhotekoshi flood into operation. Earlier, Chairperson of Ujyalo Nepal Party, Kulman Ghising, met with Prime Minister Shah. On the occasion, they discussed the matters related to ongoing rescue and relief operation in flood-hit areas, it is shared.

headline: NMB Capital Contributes Rs. 1.5 Million to PM Disaster Relief Fund for Flood Recovery
body:
NMB Capital Limited has contributed NPR 1.5 million to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund to support families affected by the recent devastating floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers.

In addition, NMB Capital employees raised funds individually to purchase essential relief materials, which were handed over to the Management Division under the Department of Health Services in Teku.

The company also expressed condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and wished for the safe rescue and recovery of those affected.

The government has also declared Bhadra 22 as a National Day of Mourning in memory of those who lost their lives in the Rasuwa floods.

To support the recovery of flood-affected individuals, industries and businesses in Rasuwa, the government will introduce an integrated business recovery plan that includes tax and customs-duty relief along with other support measures.

The Cabinet has also approved the import of 25,000 metric tonnes of sugar through Salt Trading Corporation and Food Management and Trading Company at a 1% customs duty. Security personnel involved in post-flood search and rescue operations will receive risk allowances and meal expenses. Those injured during the operations will receive free medical treatment, while the families of personnel who die in the line of duty will receive Rs.10 crores.

headline: Cabinet Unveils 7 Key Decisions, Approves $5 Million ADB Grant for Flood Relief
body:
The government has made public seven key decisions taken by the Council of Ministers during its meeting held on Thursday afternoon at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. Government spokesperson Sasmit Pokharel announced the decisions following the meeting.

The Cabinet decided to accept a US$5 million grant from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for life-saving operations and immediate emergency rescue and relief efforts for people affected by the Bhote Koshi floods.

The government has also decided to provide relief, tax and customs concessions, and other facilities under an integrated business recovery plan to help individuals, industries, traders and businesses affected by the Bhote Koshi River flood in Rasuwa resume operations at the earliest.

Similarly, the Cabinet approved the import of 25,000 metric tonnes of sugar through Salt Trading Corporation Limited and Food Management and Trading Company Limited by levying a 1% customs duty.

The government has further decided to provide risk allowances and meal expenses to security personnel and civil servants deployed for search and rescue operations following the Bhote Koshi flood. Personnel injured during the operation will receive free medical treatment, while the families of those who lose their lives will receive Rs. 1 million per deceased person as relief.

The Cabinet also decided to declare Bhadra 23, 2083 a nationwide public holiday on the occasion of Gen Z Martyrs’ Day.

In honour of those who lost their lives in the devastating flood that occurred on Bhadra 10, 2083 in the Bhote Koshi River along the Nepal-China border in Rasuwa, the government has decided to observe Bhadra 22 as a National Day of Mourning. On the day, the national flag will be flown at half-mast at government offices across Nepal as well as at Nepali embassies and diplomatic missions abroad.

The Cabinet also decided to promote Narayan Prasad Bhatta to the position of Secretary under the Gazetted Special Class of the Nepal Administration Service and appoint him as the Chief Secretary of the Office of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers of Koshi Province.
